scope: SIR.51.18-30: fidelity to existing pointed Kahana Hebrew, with stored Swete Greek as a separate control

source_files.role: Kahana pointed composite edition; not one manuscript or a preservation map
Stored Swete Greek published reading; all 13 YAML parallel strings match this control

interpretation_contract.target_form: Existing Kahana Hebrew wording and pointing; Greek remains a disclosed parallel literary form
interpretation_contract.rubric: Meaning and unsupported additions first, then ambiguity, literary function, naturalness, and consistency
interpretation_contract.attestation: Secure only as wording of the pinned digital editions; editorial brackets remain supplies, HTML small-number labels are not words
interpretation_contract.priority: Not assessed; no chronological weighting or claim of exhaustive Hebrew/Greek/Syriac comparison
interpretation_contract.outcome_semantics: Retain/change/hold concerns source-fidelity candidates and apparatus repair, not manuscript priority or publication approval
interpretation_contract.review_basis: One assistant's bounded source-language analysis; lexical database names in existing YAML are not new consultation receipts

records.change_scope: Supply disclosure; retain close English provisionally
records.baseline_English: I planned to improve my way[a], and I will not turn back, for I will find it.
records.own_candidate: I planned to improve my way, and I will not turn back, for I will find it.
records.morphology: חָשַׁבְתִּי Qal qatal 1cs; לְהִיטֶיב Hiphil infinitive of יטב; [דַּרְכִּי] noun with 1cs suffix, editorially supplied; אַהֲפֹךְ Qal yiqtol 1cs; אֶמְצָאֶנּוּ Qal yiqtol 1cs with 3ms object suffix.
records.reason: English follows the supplied object and nonpast verbs, but the current note discloses only Greek divergence, hiding the status of 'my way'. A 3ms suffix can refer to masculine דרך; identifying it categorically as feminine Wisdom is unnecessary.
records.counterargument: With the bracketed object absent, לְהִיטֶיב can independently mean 'to do good'; this is an alternative translation of the surviving words, not proof of the supply.
records.apparatus_candidate: 'My way' is supplied in brackets in the Kahana edition. Without this supply: 'I planned to do good'. Greek has practicing her, zeal for good, and not being ashamed; it does not attest the supplied Hebrew word.

records.change_scope: Source interpretation and English tense/lexical fidelity
records.baseline_English: My soul clung to her, and I did not turn my face away from her.
records.own_candidate: My soul longed for her, and I will not turn my face away from her.
records.own_alternative: My soul clung to her, and I will not turn my face away from her.
records.morphology: חַשְׁקָה Qal qatal 3fs agreeing with נַפְשִׁי; בָּהּ 3fs suffix; אַהֲפֹך Qal yiqtol 1cs with פָנַי fronted as object; מִמֶּנָּה 3fs suffix.
records.reason: חשק expresses desire/attachment; 'longed for' makes that sense clear. The unconverted yiqtol after לא supports continuing resolve, especially alongside vv.18 and 20; current simple past erases this distinction.
records.counterargument: Yiqtol may convey habitual past in retrospective poetry, and 'clung' can express strong attachment; therefore this is a reasoned preference, not a claim that Hebrew qatal/yiqtol map mechanically onto English tenses.
records.Greek_control: Stored Greek has the soul's completed struggle plus several additional actions, not the Hebrew face-turning clause; do not use its past forms to determine the Hebrew tense.

records.change_scope: Optional idiomatic candidate; no necessary semantic correction
records.baseline_English: I gave my soul after her, and for everlasting ages I will not turn away from her. In purity I found her, and from the beginning I acquired a heart for her.
records.own_candidate: I devoted my soul to pursuing her, and for everlasting ages I will not turn away from her. In purity I found her, and from her beginning I acquired a heart for her.
records.morphology: נָתַתִּי, מְצָאתִיהָ, קָנִיתִי qatal 1cs, the middle form with 3fs object; אַטֶּה Hiphil yiqtol 1cs of נטה; אַחֲרֶיהָ 'after her'; לָהּ and מִתְּחִלָּתָהּ have 3fs suffixes.
records.reason: Current text retains all four Hebrew clauses and the past/nonpast distinction. 'Gave my soul after her' is awkward but intelligible; the optional candidate makes devotion explicit and preserves the suffix on 'her beginning'.
records.counterargument: 'Pursuing' is explanatory and 'her beginning' remains semantically uncertain. Current 'from the beginning' is a defensible idiom, so no mandatory wording change is established.
records.Greek_control: Greek orders the heart and purity clauses differently, has μετʼ αὐτῶν, and ends 'I will not be abandoned'; Hebrew 'I will not turn away' is a different verb/agency, not Greek confirmation.

records.change_scope: Tense interpretation; retain Hebrew content placement
records.baseline_English: My inward parts burned like an oven as I looked toward her[a]; therefore I will not forsake her.
records.own_candidate: My inward parts grow hot like an oven when I look upon her; therefore I will not forsake her.
records.own_alternative: My inward parts would grow hot like an oven as I looked upon her; therefore I will not forsake her.
records.morphology: יֵחַמּוּ heating verb, yiqtol 3mp agreeing with מֵעַי; לְהַבִּיט Hiphil infinitive of נבט; בָּהּ 3fs suffix; אֶעֶזְבֶנָּה Qal yiqtol 1cs with 3fs object.
records.reason: Present/general or retrospective habitual heat are both possible; simple past 'burned' is more definite than the Hebrew form alone warrants. The infinitive's temporal rendering is interpretation, not a finite past verb. The second clause remains refusal to forsake her.
records.counterargument: The autobiographical qatal clauses nearby permit retrospective yiqtol; changing to present solely from morphology would overstate the case.
records.alignment: Greek v.21's ἐκτησάμην ἀγαθὸν κτῆμα corresponds in content to Hebrew v.22's קְנִיתִיהָ קִנְיָן טוֹב. The acquisition is not absent from this Hebrew passage; it occurs one verse later. Do not move it into Hebrew v.21.

records.change_scope: Retain English; repair alignment and stale apparatus metadata
records.baseline_English: Yahweh has given me the reward of my lips[b][a]; therefore I acquired her as a good possession.
records.own_candidate: Yahweh has given me the reward of my lips; therefore I acquired her as a good possession.
records.morphology: נָתַן Qal qatal 3ms; שְׂכַר construct with שִׂפְתוֹתָי 'my lips'; קְנִיתִיהָ Qal qatal 1cs with 3fs object; קִנְיָן טוֹב noun/adjective phrase.
records.reason: English represents the Hebrew reward and acquisition clauses. Greek v.22 instead has tongue as reward and future praise; acquisition corresponds to Greek v.21.
records.counterargument: The reward-of-lips idiom leaves its precise relation to speech/praise open; inserting 'for my praise' would resolve more than the Hebrew says.
records.apparatus_repairs: Move the 'her' marker to its actual referent; disclose Greek v.21/v.22 content alignment. Update lexical/theological 'the LORD' claims to the current Yahweh rendering without claiming new source selection.

records.change_scope: Retain English; align rationale with chosen wording
records.baseline_English: Turn to me[a], you who are simple[b], and lodge in the house of my instruction.
records.own_candidate: Turn to me, you who are simple, and lodge in the house of my instruction.
records.morphology: פְּנוּ and לִינוּ Qal imperatives 2mp; סְכָלִים plural adjective/substantive; מִדְרָשִׁי noun with 1cs suffix in construct with בֵּית.
records.reason: Invitation, plural addressees, lodging image, and 'my' instruction are retained. Greek ἀπαίδευτοι supports educational deficiency; 'simple' is defensible in this context.
records.counterargument: סכלים can be stronger ('fools'); Greek does not prove that the Hebrew lacks rebuke. 'Unlearned' is also defensible but not a necessary correction.
records.apparatus_repairs: Existing lexical/theological 'chosen' fields say 'unlearned' while English says 'simple'; synchronize the rationale rather than fabricate review of a changed text.

records.change_scope: Correct false Greek quotation in note; optional tense-explicit English
records.baseline_English: How long will you lack these things[a], while your soul is very thirsty?
records.own_candidate: How long will you lack these things, while your soul remains very thirsty?
records.morphology: עַד מָתַי 'until when/how long'; תַחְסְרוּן Qal yiqtol 2mp with extended ending; אֵלּוּ וְאֵלּוּ repeated plural demonstratives; נַפְשְׁכֶם singular noun with 2mp suffix; תִּהְיֶה Qal yiqtol 3fs agreeing with soul.
records.reason: The current main text is a plausible rhetorical rendering. Its note wrongly attributes 'How long' to stored Greek, which starts καὶ ὅτι and lacks a temporal 'until when' phrase.
records.counterargument: Greek ὅτι can be construed interrogatively 'why' or declaratively 'because/that'; do not invent a definitive Greek rhetorical form from the Hebrew.
records.apparatus_candidate: Hebrew repeats 'these and these' and uses 'will be very thirsty'. Greek has 'you say you are lacking in these things' and plural 'your souls thirst greatly'; its opening καὶ ὅτι is not the Hebrew 'How long'.

records.change_scope: Correct demonstrably false bilingual pronoun note; retain English
records.baseline_English: I opened my mouth and spoke of her: acquire wisdom for yourselves without silver[a].
records.own_candidate: I opened my mouth and spoke of her: acquire wisdom for yourselves without silver.
records.morphology: פָתַחְתִּי Qal qatal 1cs; דִבַּרְתִּי Piel qatal 1cs; בָהּ preposition with 3fs suffix; קְנוּ Qal imperative 2mp; לָכֶם preposition with 2mp suffix; חָכְמָה explicit noun.
records.reason: Hebrew has feminine 'of her' and names wisdom. Stored Greek ἐλάλησα has no pronoun attached to 'spoke', and its αὐτοῖς is masculine/neuter dative plural, not feminine singular. Thus 'Hebrew and Greek both use a feminine pronoun here' is false.
records.counterargument: Greek's elliptical acquisition may refer contextually to instruction/wisdom; that contextual referent does not supply a missing feminine pronoun or an explicit σοφία.
records.apparatus_candidate: Hebrew has 'spoke of her' and explicitly 'wisdom'; stored Swete Greek has 'spoke' and an elliptical 'Acquire ... without silver', with αὐτοῖς rather than the Hebrew 'for yourselves'. No Greek source emendation is proposed.

records.change_scope: Retain substance; optional plural clarity and fuller Greek disclosure
records.baseline_English: Bring your neck under her yoke[a], and let your soul bear her burden. She is near to those who seek her, and the one who gives himself finds her.
records.own_candidate: Bring your necks under her yoke, and let your soul bear her burden. She is near to those who seek her, and the one who gives himself finds her.
records.morphology: צַוְּארֵיכֶם plural necks with 2mp suffix; הָבִיאוּ Hiphil imperative 2mp; תִּשָּׂא Qal yiqtol 3fs, volitional in exhortation, agreeing with נַפְשְׁכֶם; נוֹתֵן and מוֹצֵא Qal participles ms; נַפְשׁוֹ 'his soul/life'.
records.reason: Current substance is coherent Hebrew; 'gives himself' reasonably expresses giving one's soul/life. Plural 'necks' is closer than a collective singular but no consequential semantic error is established.
records.counterargument: 'Under' interprets Hebrew ב in the yoke image; singular 'your neck' is an ordinary English distributive and agrees with Greek's singular neck.
records.Greek_control: Greek says receive instruction and 'it is near to find her'; it does not spell out Hebrew's seekers or final self-giving finder. Its difference should not be reduced solely to 'burden/instruction'.

records.change_scope: Hold small/young interpretation; correct stale pronoun note and rationale
records.baseline_English: See with your own eyes that I was young[b][a], and I stood by her and found her.
records.own_candidate: See with your own eyes that I was small, and I stood by her and found her.
records.own_alternative: See with your own eyes that I was young, and I stood by her and found her.
records.morphology: רְאוּ Qal imperative 2mp; קָטֹן adjective 'small/little', potentially age/status; הָיִיתִי Qal qatal 1cs; עָמַדְתִּי Qal qatal 1cs; בָהּ 3fs suffix; מְצָאתִיהָ Qal qatal 1cs with 3fs object.
records.reason: 'Small' preserves age/status ambiguity; 'young' is contextually possible beside v.28's youth. Either requires a consistent rationale. The current note falsely says the main text uses 'it', although both objects are 'her'.
records.counterargument: 'Small' can misleadingly suggest bodily size in English, while autobiographical youth elsewhere supports 'young'; no source-only evidence uniquely settles the choice.
records.apparatus_repairs: Correct the pronoun note to match 'her'; synchronize lexical and theological choices. Greek 'I labored little ... much rest' changes predicate and object, not merely קטון's lexical sense.

records.change_scope: Correct subject/person and verbal force; synchronize notes/rationales
records.baseline_English: Many heard my instruction in my youth[b][a], and they acquired silver and gold by me.
records.own_candidate: Many heard my instruction in my youth, and you will acquire silver and gold through me.
records.own_alternative: Many heard my instruction in my youth; acquire silver and gold through me.
records.morphology: שָׁמְעוּ Qal qatal 3cp with רַבִּים subject; לִמּוּדִי noun with 1cs suffix; בִּנְעֻרוֹתָי youth noun with 1cs suffix; תִּקְנוּ Qal yiqtol 2mp of קנה, not qatal 3cp; בִי preposition with 1cs suffix.
records.reason: The pointed verb changes addressee from third-person many to second-person plural you. Current 'they acquired' replaces both person and aspect. 'You will acquire' preserves the form; the imperative alternative expresses exhortative yiqtol as an English injunction, without repointing it to Hebrew קְנוּ.
records.counterargument: Context of commands and Greek κτήσασθε support exhortative English 'acquire'; a promissory future is not uniquely compelled. Neither supports retaining third-person past.
records.apparatus_repairs: Withdraw the assertion that Hebrew is wholly declarative about others gaining wealth. The first clause is retrospective; the second addresses you in yiqtol. Align the existing 'through me' rationale and note with the actual chosen phrase, and relocate notes to their clauses. Greek has two imperatives and different first-clause wording; it does not prove Hebrew imperative morphology.

records.change_scope: Retain pointed old-age interpretation; reconcile song preposition rationale
records.baseline_English: May my soul rejoice in my old age[a], and may you not be put to shame by my song.
records.own_candidate: May my soul rejoice in my old age, and may you not be ashamed in my song.
records.morphology: תִּשְׂמַח Qal yiqtol 3fs agreeing with נַפְשִׁי, capable of jussive wish; בְּשֵׂיבָתִי pointed שֵׂיבָה 'gray hair/old age' with 1cs suffix; תֵבוֹשוּ Qal yiqtol 2mp of בוש; בְּשִׁירָתִי 'in/by my song'.
records.reason: 'Old age' is supported by the exact pointing; a return/repentance interpretation would require a changed analysis/pointing and is not warranted here. Greek optatives support a wish as a control, while its soul/mercy/praise referents differ from Hebrew.
records.counterargument: Hebrew לא plus yiqtol also permits an assurance ('you will not be ashamed'); Greek is not proof of Hebrew mood. 'By my song' is a possible instrumental reading of ב; 'in my song' retains a broader relation.
records.apparatus_repairs: Keep old-age disclosure. Existing chosen 'in my song' conflicts with actual 'by my song'; reconcile this and the revision history without rewriting historical receipts. Qal בוש is not a Hebrew passive stem even when English uses 'be put to shame'.

records.change_scope: Retain English; repair note anchoring and disclose separate Greek content
records.baseline_English: Do your work in righteousness[a], and he will give you your reward in its time. Blessed is Yahweh forever, and praised is his name from generation to generation.
records.own_candidate: Do your work in righteousness, and he will give you your reward in its time. Blessed is Yahweh forever, and praised is his name from generation to generation.
records.morphology: מַעֲשֵׂיכֶם plural deeds with 2mp suffix; עֲשׂוּ Qal imperative 2mp; נוֹתֵן Qal participle ms with explicit הוּא; בְּעִתּוֹ 'at its/his time'; בָּרוּךְ passive participle/adjective; מְשֻׁבָּח Pual participle ms.
records.reason: Promissory 'will give' is a contextual rendering of the participle, consistent with the reward's appointed time; no mandatory tense correction. The Hebrew doxology is actually in the pinned source and should remain in this working form.
records.counterargument: The time suffix can refer to reward or God; current 'its' selects one reference, already acknowledged by the note. 'Gives' is also defensible for the participle.
records.apparatus_repairs: Move the time-alternative marker from righteousness to 'its time'. Disclose Greek πρὸ καιροῦ ('before the time') instead of Hebrew righteousness, and the absence of the Hebrew doxology in this stored Greek verse. Align old 'the LORD' lexical metadata with Yahweh. No conclusion about original inclusion follows.

batch_summary.summary_review_correction: Independent review distinguished verse 28's demonstrable pointed-source person mismatch from verse 19's interpretive future preference. Original per-record candidates and counterarguments remain unchanged; no application is approved.
batch_summary.existing_provenance_debt: SIR.51.19 and SIR.51.20 lack ai_draft and translation.philosophy in the pinned records. No original generation metadata is inferred or invented here.
batch_summary.pointing_limit: Morphology follows the stored Kahana vowels; an unpointed consonantal witness may permit other analyses. No change to those vowels is proposed, and secure digital-edition wording is not secure ancient vocalization.
batch_summary.next_gate: Review frozen candidates and disagreements before any canonical application; preserve all source/rights and record-integrity gates
